questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Opening classification — match — 1) Extrahepatic 2) Intrahepatic pre-sinusoidal 3) Post hepatic … A) 3rd order vein B) 1st order portal vein involvement C) Hepatic venous obstruction
questions.exp: Extrahepatic: 1st order portal vein involvement; Pre-sinusoidal: 3rd order vein; Post hepatic: hepatic venous obstruction. (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Fill up: The extrahepatic entity is Extrahepatic portal vein occlusion (______), described as ______.
questions.exp: 'Extrahepatic portal vein occlusion (EHPVO). • Non cirrhotic'. (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Intrahepatic sub-types — match — 1) Pre-sinusoidal 2) Sinusoidal 3) Post-sinusoidal … A) Cirrhosis PH B) Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (veno-occlusive) C) Non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis (NCPF)
questions.exp: Pre-sinusoidal: 3rd order vein, NCPF; Sinusoidal: Cirrhosis PH; Post sinusoidal: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (veno occlusive). (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Post-hepatic hepatic venous obstruction is exemplified by which condition, and what does the arrow beneath it lead to?
questions.exp: 'Post hepatic: Hepatic venous obstruction: • Budd Chiari syndrome → Cirrhosis.' (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Fill up (BCS pathogenesis): Vasculature — ______ ductule of acinus → right atrium; hepatic venous occlusion / thrombosis anywhere → ______ entry into right atrium.
questions.exp: 'Vasculature : efferent ductule of acinus — Hepatic venous occlusion / Thrombosis anywhere → IVC entry into Right atrium.' (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Site of BCS — match — 1) Hepatic vein 2) Terminal IVC … A) 2nd most common B) Most common
questions.exp: 'Hepatic vein : m/c. Terminal IVC : 2nd m/c.' (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Among the inherited deficiencies causing BCS, which hierarchy is printed?
opts: Factor V Leiden > Prothrombin gene > Protein C
questions.exp: 'Deficiency : Anti thrombin 3 > Protein C/Protein S.' (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six printed causes of BCS?
questions.exp: Causes: Factor V Leiden mutation; deficiency AT3 > protein C/S; MPN; polycythemia rubra vera (PCRV); PNH; pregnancy/post partum. (Book p1033)

questions.sec: Classification of hepatic vascular disease; BCS pathogenesis, site, causes, classification
questions.q: Classification of BCS — judge: I Secondary is far commoner than primary (2° >> 1°). II Secondary is subdivided into inherited and acquired.
questions.exp: 'Primary / Secondary (2° >> 1°) → Inherited / Acquired.' (Book p1033)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Most common presentation demographic of BCS printed?
questions.exp: 'm/c : 30–40 years post partum female.' (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Fill up: Ascites in BCS arises from zone ______ involvement → sinusoidal ______ + pooling.
questions.exp: 'Ascites : zone 3 involvement → sinusoidal distension + pooling.' (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Subacute BCS — judge: I It is the most common presentation. II It causes refractory ascites with collaterals. III The ascites is high-SAAG, high-protein.
opts: I and II true, III false
II and III true, I false
I true, II and III false
questions.exp: '1. Subacute : m/c presentation; Refractory ascites + collaterals; High SAAG, high protein ascites.' (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: A patient's ascitic fluid shows high SAAG and LOW protein. Per the Note on this page, what does this pattern indicate?
opts: Post-sinusoidal (hepatic venous) cause such as BCS
questions.exp: 'Note : High SAAG, low protein ascites : Sinusoidal cause.' (BCS gives high SAAG, high protein.) (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Acute hepatitis presentation of BCS: what jaundice frequency is printed and how common is fulminant hepatic failure?
opts: Jaundice universal; fulminant hepatic failure rare
questions.exp: '2. Acute Hepatitis : Abdominal pain + hepatomegaly + ascites; Jaundice : <10% patients; Fulminant hepatic failure : Rare.' Then '3. Cirrhosis'. (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Prognosis of BCS as printed?
questions.exp: 'PROGNOSIS • very poor : 3yr survival rate < 10%.' (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Mechanism flowchart, LEFT column — put in order: A) Extravasation of fluid from hepatic vein > sinusoids B) Increased sinusoidal & portal pressure C) High SAAG, high protein ascites D) Sinusoidal distension
questions.exp: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction → Increased sinusoidal & portal pressure → Sinusoidal distension → Extravasation of fluid from hepatic vein > sinusoids → High SAAG, high protein ascites. (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Mechanism flowchart, RIGHT column — put in order: A) Fibrosis, nodular regenerative hyperplasia B) Venous stasis and congestion C) Hepatocyte necrosis (centrilobular) leading to lobar collapse D) Hypoxic damage to hepatocytes, zone 3 involvement
questions.exp: Venous stasis and congestion → Hypoxic damage to hepatocytes, zone 3 → Hepatocyte necrosis (centrilobular) leading to lobar collapse → Fibrosis, nodular regenerative hyperplasia → Cirrhosis. Caption: 'mechanism of Ascites & Cirrhosis in BCS'. (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Investigations — match — 1) Hepatic venous Doppler 2) CECT 3) MRI … A) IOC B) Nodules / hemorrhagic liver C) Screening test; obstruction + portosystemic collaterals
questions.exp: Doppler: screening test, obstruction + portosystemic collaterals; CECT: IOC; MRI: nodules/hemorrhagic liver. (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: What does the red arrow on the 'CECT image in BCS' point to?
questions.exp: Label: 'Caudate lobe hypertrophy' — CECT image in BCS. (Book p1034)

questions.sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management
questions.q: Management of BCS: which statement matches the printed text?
opts: Angioplasty is reserved for decompensated patients; anticoagulation is optional
Liver transplant is first-line in all non-decompensated patients
Anticoagulation is mandatory for all; non-decompensated patients get angioplasty ± stenting, and on failure TIPSS
Anticoagulation only if PNH; all others go straight to TIPSS
questions.exp: 'mandatory anticoagulation to all. Non decompensated patients : Angioplasty +/− stenting —Failure→ TIPSS (Transjugular Intrahepatic Porto-systemic Shunt).' (Book p1034)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Fill up the alternative names in the table header: NCPF / IPH / Hepatoportal ______ / Obliterative portal ______.
questions.exp: Header: 'NCPF/IPH/Hepatoportal Sclerosis Obliterative portal venopathy)'. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Row 'Outcome' (demographic) — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) 20–40 yr adult Asian male B) 3–8 yr child (m/c cause of UGI bleed in children)
questions.exp: EHPVO: 3–8 yr child (m/c cause of UGI bleed in children); NCPF: 20–40 yr adult Asian male. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Rows 'Involvement' and 'Cause' — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) 3rd order portal vein; E. coli / arsenic associations, hypervitaminosis A B) 1st order portal vein; umbilical sepsis > prothrombotic state
questions.exp: EHPVO: 1st order portal vein, umbilical sepsis > prothrombotic state. NCPF: 3rd order portal vein, E. coli/arsenic, hypervitaminosis A. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: A 6-year-old presents with massive haematemesis and a massive spleen; blood counts show anaemia and thrombocytopenia. Per the table, what explains the cytopenias and which condition is this?
questions.exp: EHPVO presentation: 'massive UGI bleed + massive spleen (hypersplenism) → Anemia, thrombocytopenia'. NCPF presents similarly but in 20–40 yr adults. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Row 'Prognosis' — judge: I EHPVO prognosis is good with no risk for cirrhosis. II NCPF prognosis is good with negligible risk for cirrhosis.
questions.exp: EHPVO: 'Good, with no risk for cirrhosis'; NCPF: 'Good, negligible risk for cirrhosis'. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Row 'Investigations' — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) IOC Doppler; biopsy (gold standard) shows obliterative portal venopathy B) IOC CT; cavernoma appearance of collaterals
questions.exp: EHPVO: IOC CT, cavernoma appearance of collaterals. NCPF: IOC Doppler, biopsy gold std — obliterative portal venopathy. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Fill up (EHPVO complications): Stunted growth and portal ______ — compression of the biliary system by portal ______.
questions.exp: 'Portal biliopathy : compression of biliary system by portal collaterals.' NCPF complications: '—'. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: What treatment is printed for EHPVO, and what is printed for NCPF?
opts: EHPVO: mandatory anticoagulation; NCPF: splenectomy with devascularisation
Both: angioplasty ± stenting, then endoscopic sclerotherapy on failure
EHPVO: endoscopic variceal ligation / endoscopic sclerotherapy; NCPF: '—' (none printed)
EHPVO: TIPSS after failed angioplasty; NCPF: liver transplant (only treatment)
questions.exp: Treatment row: EHPVO = Endoscopic variceal ligation / Endoscopic sclerotherapy; NCPF = '—'. (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Note on the most common cause of portal hypertension — 1) Asia 2) World … A) Biliary atresia B) EHPVO
questions.exp: 'm/c cause of PHTN : Asia: EHPVO; world: Biliary atresia.' (Book p1035)

questions.sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images
questions.q: Match — 1) CECT panels 2) Colour Doppler 3) Trichrome/H&E micrograph … A) Obliterative portal venopathy — sclerotic & non-patent portal tracts B) EHPVO showing collaterals C) EHPVO with cavernoma labelled
questions.exp: 'CECT: EHPVO showing collaterals'; 'Color doppler : EHPVO' with 'Cavernoma' arrow; 'Obliterative portal venopathy' with 'Sclerotic & non patent portal tracts'. (Book p1035)
